Brahim Díaz set up the only goal of Morocco's 1–0 win over Niger on Tuesday, giving the Real Madrid forward an assist in both meetings between the sides during this international break. Three days after his cross found Yassir Zabiri for the opener in a 5–1 win, it was a backheel from Brahim that made the difference in Rabat:
 Playing as the No. 10 in Mohamed Ouahbi's 4-2-3-1, Brahim combined with Abdellah Ouazane midway through the first half. Ouazane played the ball into Brahim, whose first-time backheel found him again inside the penalty area. The youngster took a touch and finished to mark his first senior start for Morocco with a goal. Brahim played 84 minutes and completed 90% of his passes.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Niger were the designated home side despite the match taking place in Morocco. They saw just 32% of the ball but twice threatened to equalize after halftime. An offside decision ruled out one effort, and Yassine Bounou denied Youssouf Oumarou in the 55th minute. Morocco put eight of their 13 shots on target but never added to Ouazane's goal.
 The win gives Morocco 12 points from four matches in 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying, six clear of second-placed Gabon.
